stimulus.note: theta and phi are the inputs this generator passes to ffsim. They are not a convention. The convention is the matrix ffsim returns.

serialization: Each amplitude is [re, im]. Each part is round(x, 12), and a part that rounds to zero is written as 0.0 so the sign of zero cannot drift.
assembly: Column j of a gate matrix is the statevector of computational-basis vector j. The script builds the one-hot ffsim sector vector at the address whose ffsim.qiskit.ffsim_vec_to_qiskit_vec image is j, calls the recorded function, and embeds the result with the same function. matrix[row][col] is the amplitude of basis state row in that image. Basis bitstrings are ffsim.addresses_to_strings; qiskit_index is where ffsim_vec_to_qiskit_vec placed the one-hot. No amplitude under gates or jordan_wigner is computed by this script. jordan_wigner terms are sorted by Pauli label for a stable encoding; z_qubits is the indices where that term's qiskit Pauli.z is true.

source.obtained_by: source read at that commit; the package was not installed and not executed

wire_is_mode.quote: In this setting, each wire in a quantum circuit describes a fermionic mode. Upon measurement, each mode can be found to be occupied by a single particle (1) or be empty (0).

spin_blocks.quote: The fermions might also come in several distinguishable species, as is the case when they carry a spin degree of freedom. In this case, each spatial mode of an experiment can be occupied by a particle of each spin state. In the circuit description, each individual mode is assigned its own wire. For example, a system of spin-1/2 fermions in four spatial modes is described by a circuit with eight wires where the first four wires denote the spin-up and the last four wires denote the spin-down modes.

wire_index_formula.reading: Species i, site j is wire i * sites + j. The first register is spin_0, so species 0 occupies the first block of wires.

sequential_not_interleaved.quote:
For example, a sequential register [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] with two species implies that wires 0, 1, 2 are of the same type while an interleaved ordering implies that wires 0, 2, and 4 are of the same type.
Possible conventions are "sequential", where the first num_sites wires denote the first species, the second num_sites wires denote the second species etc., and "interleaved", where the first num_species wires denote the first site, the second num_species wires denote the second site etc.

first_block_is_alpha.quote:
occ_a, occ_b = set(), set()
occupations = [occ_a, occ_b]
...
spin, orb = divmod(circuit.qubits.index(q), norb)
...
spin_a, orb_a = divmod(a, norb)
spin_b, orb_b = divmod(b, norb)
spins = (ffsim.Spin.ALPHA, ffsim.Spin.BETA)
first_block_is_alpha.reading: Wire index // norb is the species. Species 0 is stored as alpha (ffsim.Spin.ALPHA) and species 1 as beta. Together with the module text that the first wires are spin-up, the first block is spin-up / alpha.

adapter_reverses_orbital_index_before_ca.quote:
spin, orb = divmod(circuit.qubits.index(q), norb)
# reverse index due to qiskit convention
occupations[spin].add(norb - 1 - orb)
...
# reverse orbitals due to qiskit convention
alpha_orbs = [norb - 1 - orb for orb in alpha_orbs]
adapter_reverses_orbital_index_before_ca.reading: That reversal lives in qiskit-cold-atom's adapter, on the way into ffsim. The gate matrices in this file pass orbital indices through unchanged. ffsim.qiskit.jordan_wigner places number_operator(0, Spin.ALPHA) on z_qubits [0] and number_operator(0, Spin.BETA) on z_qubits [norb] (see jordan_wigner). That is the block quote — site j of the first block on wire j — and not the adapter's norb-1-orb flip. A later phase that copies the flip will disagree with these matrices.

spinless_2/num_orb0.note: FermionicQASM num on mode 0. Spinless: nelec is an int, and the spin argument is not passed.

spinless_2/num_orb1.note: FermionicQASM num on the last mode. Pins which orbital takes the phase.

spinless_2/givens_0_1.note: FermionicQASM givens on modes 0, 1. phi is passed as 0.0 (the one-parameter gate).

spinless_2/tunnel_0_1.note: FermionicQASM tunnel on modes 0, 1. The sign is whatever this call returns.

spinless_2/numnum_1_0.note: Same call with the orbital pair reversed, so pair order is pinned rather than assumed.

spinless_2/givens_1_0.note: Givens with the orbital pair reversed. (0, 1) and (1, 0) are different calls.

spinless_2/tunnel_1_0.note: Tunnel with the orbital pair reversed.

spinless_3/num_orb0.note: FermionicQASM num on mode 0. Spinless: nelec is an int, and the spin argument is not passed.

spinless_3/num_orb2.note: FermionicQASM num on the last mode. Pins which orbital takes the phase.

spinless_3/givens_0_1.note: FermionicQASM givens on modes 0, 1. phi is passed as 0.0 (the one-parameter gate).

spinless_3/tunnel_0_1.note: FermionicQASM tunnel on modes 0, 1. The sign is whatever this call returns.

spinless_3/numnum_0_2.note: numnum on non-adjacent modes 0, 2. ffsim accepts it; number operators carry no hop.

spinless_3/givens_0_2.note: givens on non-adjacent orbitals 0, 2. ffsim applies it. F4.2 still refuses that statement through fermion::givens_expr; this matrix is the semantic pin for when a routing lands, not a lowering to ship.

spinless_3/tunnel_0_2.note: tunnel on non-adjacent orbitals 0, 2, same status as givens_0_2.

spinless_4/num_orb0.note: FermionicQASM num on mode 0. Spinless: nelec is an int, and the spin argument is not passed.

spinless_4/num_orb3.note: FermionicQASM num on the last mode. Pins which orbital takes the phase.

spinless_4/givens_0_1.note: FermionicQASM givens on modes 0, 1. phi is passed as 0.0 (the one-parameter gate).

spinless_4/tunnel_0_1.note: FermionicQASM tunnel on modes 0, 1. The sign is whatever this call returns.

spinless_4/numnum_0_2.note: numnum on non-adjacent modes 0, 2. ffsim accepts it; number operators carry no hop.

spinless_4/givens_0_2.note: givens on non-adjacent orbitals 0, 2. ffsim applies it. F4.2 still refuses that statement through fermion::givens_expr; this matrix is the semantic pin for when a routing lands, not a lowering to ship.

spinless_4/tunnel_0_2.note: tunnel on non-adjacent orbitals 0, 2, same status as givens_0_2.

spinful_2/num_orb0_alpha.note: num on alpha orbital 0 only. One wire in the first block, not both species.

spinful_2/num_orb0_beta.note: num on beta orbital 0 only. One wire in the second block.

spinful_2/num_orb1_alpha.note: num on alpha orbital 1. Within the alpha block, orbital index 1, not a reversed index.

spinful_2/numnum_0_1_alpha.note: numnum inside the alpha species, spatial orbitals 0 and 1. Not the opposite-spin term.

spinful_2/givens_0_1_alpha.note: givens inside alpha. Spin.ALPHA does not also rotate beta.

spinful_2/onsite_orb0.note: Opposite spins, same spatial orbital. This is the ffsim call for numnum between the two wires of one site, not apply_num_num_interaction.

spinful_2/numprod_alpha0_beta1.note: Opposite spins, different spatial orbitals: alpha 0 with beta 1. apply_num_op_prod_interaction, not apply_num_num_interaction.

not_a_pin.reason: The docstring of ffsim.apply_givens_rotation prints a 4x4 Jordan-Wigner matrix whose off-diagonal signs are swapped relative to gates['spinless_2/givens_0_1'] in this file (phi=0, basis order 00, 01, 10, 11 as ffsim.addresses_to_strings and ffsim_vec_to_qiskit_vec recorded them). The matrix is the pin. Editing the fixture to match the docstring would put the wrong sign into F4.2.

does_not_block: F4.2 same-spin givens, tunnel, num, and numnum
unpinned.reason: ffsim.apply_givens_rotation and ffsim.apply_tunneling_interaction take a Spin flag and act inside that species. Neither call mixes an alpha orbital with a beta orbital. This generator does not synthesize a cross-spin matrix from some other operator. A FermionicQASM givens or tunnel whose wires sit in different spin blocks — including the adjacent pair across the block boundary, m[N-1], m[N] — has no ffsim matrix in this file. F4.3 must not treat same-spin agreement as covering that case. F4.2 can still lower it through fermion::givens_expr; the QASM2+rbs lane is the oracle for that lowering, and it is not an ffsim pin.
